property.name: http.agent.name
property.description:
HTTP 'User-Agent' request header. MUST NOT be empty - please set this to a single word uniquely related to your organization.
NOTE: You should also check other related properties:
http.robots.agents http.agent.description http.agent.url http.agent.email http.agent.version
and set their values appropriately.

property.name: linkdb.ignore.internal.links
property.description: If true, when adding new links to a page, links from the same host are ignored. This is an effective way to limit the size of the link database, keeping only the highest quality links.

property.name: db.ignore.external.links
property.description: If true,meta_ outlinks leading from a page to external hosts or domain will be ignored. This is an effective way to limit the crawl to include only initially injected hosts or domains, without creating complex URLFilters. See 'db.ignore.external.links.mode'.

property.name: plugin.includes
property.description: Regular expression naming plugin directory names to include. Any plugin not matching this expression is excluded. By default Nutch includes plugins to crawl HTML and various other document formats via HTTP/HTTPS and indexing the crawled content into Solr. More plugins are available to support more indexing backends, to fetch ftp:// and file:// URLs, for focused crawling, and many other use cases.

property.name: anchorIndexingFilter.deduplicate
property.description: With this enabled the indexer will case-insensitive deduplicate anchors before indexing. This prevents possible hundreds or thousands of identical anchors for a given page to be indexed but will affect the search scoring (i.e. tf=1.0f).

property.name: file.content.limit
property.description: The length limit for downloaded content using the file:// protocol, in bytes. If this value is non-negative (>=0), content longer than it will be truncated; otherwise, no truncation at all. Do not confuse this setting with the http.content.limit setting.

property.name: parser.skip.truncated
property.description: Boolean value for whether we should skip parsing for truncated documents. By default this property is activated due to extremely high levels of CPU which parsing can sometimes take.

property.name: db.fetch.interval.default
property.description: The default number of seconds between re-fetches of a page (30 days).

property.name: db.max.outlinks.per.page
property.description: The maximum number of outlinks that we'll process for a page. If this value is nonnegative (>=0), at most db.max.outlinks.per.page outlinks will be processed for a page; otherwise, all outlinks will be processed.

property.name: http.content.limit
property.description: The length limit for downloaded content using the http/https protocols, in bytes. If this value is non-negative (>=0), content longer than it will be truncated; otherwise, no truncation at all. Do not confuse this setting with the file.content.limit setting.

property.name: metatags.names
property.description: Names of the metatags to extract, separated by ',meta_'. Use '*' to extract all metatags. Prefixes the names with 'meta_' in the parse-metadata. For instance to index description and keywords, you need to activate the plugin index-metadata and set the value of the parameter 'index.parse.md' to 'meta_description,meta_metatag.keywords'.

property.name: db.update.max.inlinks
property.description: Maximum number of inlinks to take into account when updating a URL score in the crawlDB. Only the best scoring inlinks are kept.

property.name: generate.max.count
property.description: The maximum number of URLs in a single fetchlist. -1 if unlimited. The URLs are counted according to the value of the parameter generate.count.mode.

property.name: fetcher.server.delay
property.description: The number of seconds the fetcher will delay between successive requests to the same server. Note that this might get overridden by a Crawl-Delay from a robots.txt and is used ONLY if fetcher.threads.per.queue is set to 1.

property.name: fetcher.threads.fetch
property.description: The number of FetcherThreads the fetcher should use. This is also determines the maximum number of requests that are made at once (each FetcherThread handles one connection). The total number of threads running in distributed mode will be the number of fetcher threads * number of nodes as fetcher has one map task per node.

property.name: fetcher.threads.per.queue
property.description: This number is the maximum number of threads that should be allowed to access a queue at one time. Setting it to a value > 1 will cause the Crawl-Delay value from robots.txt to be ignored and the value of fetcher.server.min.delay to be used as a delay between successive requests to the same server instead of fetcher.server.delay.

property.name: fetcher.timelimit.mins
property.description: This is the number of minutes allocated to the fetching. Once this value is reached, any remaining entry from the input URL list is skipped and all active queues are emptied. The default value of -1 deactivates the time limit.

property.name: fetcher.maxNum.threads
property.description: Max number of fetch threads allowed when using fetcher.bandwidth.target. Defaults to fetcher.threads.fetch if unspecified or set to a value lower than it.

property.name: db.max.anchor.length
property.description: The maximum number of characters permitted in an anchor.

property.name: index.parse.md
property.description: Comma-separated list of keys to be taken from the parse metadata to generate fields. Can be used e.g. for 'description' or 'keywords' provided that these values are generated by a parser (see parse-metatags plugin)

property.name: index.metadata.separator
property.description: Separator to use if you want to index multiple values for a given field. Leave empty to treat each value as a single value.

property.name: index.metadata.multivalued.fields
property.description: Comma-separated list of dynamic-navigations-multivalue-fields to be taken from the parse metadata to generate fields.

property.name: indexer.delete.robots.noindex
property.description: Whether the indexer will delete documents marked by robots=noindex

property.name: indexer.delete.skipped.by.indexingfilter
property.description: Whether the indexer will delete documents that were skipped by indexing filters

property.name: fetcher.threads.per.host
property.description: Does not apply to nutch v1.x

property.name: db.ignore.internal.links
property.description:
If true, outlinks leading from a page to internal hosts or domain will be ignored. This is an effective way to limit the crawl to include only initially injected hosts or domains, without creating complex URLFilters. See 'db.ignore.external.links.mode'.
*************************************************** NOTE *************************************************** Using OSSearch Nutch 2.x setting while testing Nutch 1.x this prevented nutch from crawling anything other then urls in seed file. i.e. one url in seed file after 50 rounds only one url was indexed to solr!!!! So use the Nutch 1.x default value!

property.name: db.max.outlink.length
property.description: The maximum length in characters accepted for outlinks before applying URL normalizers and filters. If this value is nonnegative (>=0), only URLs with a length in characters less or equal than db.max.outlink.length are accepted and then passed to URL normalizers and filters. Doing the length check beforehand avoids that normalizers or filters hang up on overlong URLs. Note: this property is only used to check URLs found as outlinks and redirects, but not for injected URLs.

property.name: hadoop.tmp.dir
property.description: To configure Hadoop to use a different place than /tmp for temporary files, a place where you have enough disk space to fit all downloaded and temporary data. You can configure this by adding this to conf/hadoop-site.xml when running a Hadoop cluster (non-local mode). (if you run Hadoop in non-local mode, you need to restart the cluster) For "local" crawls: - do not share this folder for two simultaneously running Nutch jobs - you have to clean-up the temp folder, esp. after failed jobs (if no job is currently running with this folder defined as hadoop.tmp.dir a clean-up is save) Successful jobs do not leave any data in temp except for empty directories.

property.name: mapreduce.task.io.sort.mb
property.description: Hadoop property (not a Nutch property): the size, in megabytes, of the in-memory buffer used while sorting map output. Hadoop default is 100. The sort-heavy crawl steps (updatedb, dedup, invertlinks) spill to disk and merge far less with a larger buffer. Each concurrently running map task allocates its own buffer, so JVM heap must accommodate (buffer size x parallel local map tasks).

property.name: mapreduce.task.io.sort.factor
property.description: Hadoop property (not a Nutch property): the number of spill file streams merged at once when sorting map output or merging reduce inputs. Hadoop default is 10. A higher value reduces the number of merge passes for large sorts (e.g. crawldb updates).

property.name: mapreduce.local.map.tasks.maximum
property.description: Hadoop property (not a Nutch property): maximum number of map tasks the LocalJobRunner executes in parallel PER JOB. Hadoop's default is 1, which serializes every map task onto a single core. Applies to all crawl steps EXCEPT the index step, where the crawler forces this to 1 because concurrent indexing maps caused Solr commit failures. Each concurrently running map allocates its own sort buffer (mapreduce.task.io.sort.mb), so JVM heap must accommodate (sort buffer x this value x concurrent crawls).

property.name: mapreduce.local.reduce.tasks.maximum
property.description: Hadoop property (not a Nutch property): maximum number of reduce tasks the LocalJobRunner executes in parallel. Hadoop's default is 1. Applies to all crawl steps EXCEPT the index step, where the crawler forces this to 1 (see mapreduce.local.map.tasks.maximum). Each concurrent reduce buffers shuffle data in the shared JVM heap (see mapreduce.reduce.shuffle.input.buffer.percent) - lower this value if crawl steps fail under memory pressure.

property.name: mapreduce.reduce.shuffle.input.buffer.percent
property.description: Hadoop property (not a Nutch property): fraction of JVM heap EACH reduce task may use to buffer shuffled map output. Hadoop's default is 0.70, which assumes one reduce per JVM. OSSearch runs ALL crawls as LocalJobRunner jobs inside ONE JVM shared with the Spring Boot application, so the worst case is (concurrent crawls x mapreduce.local.reduce.tasks.maximum x this value) of the heap. 0.70 exhausted memory on a single large shuffle (observed: linkdb invert of a 13k-page segment killed the job). At 0.02 with 2 reduces per job, 10 concurrent crawls budget at most 40% of the heap; excess shuffle data spills to disk, which is cheap on local SSD storage (keep hadoop.tmp.dir OFF NFS).

property.name: mapreduce.map.output.compress.codec
property.description: Hadoop property (not a Nutch property): the compression codec for intermediate map output (mapreduce.map.output.compress is enabled by the crawler). Hadoop's default DefaultCodec (zlib) is CPU-expensive; Snappy is much faster and runs pure-Java via the snappy-java library bundled on the classpath (Hadoop 3.3.1+), so no native Hadoop libraries are needed. Do NOT use Lz4Codec: lz4-java is not on the classpath.

property.name: parser.html.outlinks.include_tags
property.description: Comma separated list of CSS like tags, from which outlinks should be extracted in addition to the defaults provided by Nutch. Nutch by default takes links from: a, area, form, frame, iframe, script, link, img, source. It is required to only specify the element type, and its class name ('.'). More complex expressions will not be parsed. Valid examples: outline-button.button-url,someOtherElementType.someOtherElementAttribute Invalid expressions: div#head#part1,#footer,.inner#post

property.name: parser.html.blacklist
property.value: div.edan-facets,div.edan-search-facets,nasm-facet-dropdown,div#collections-trail,div.col span_3_of_12 robots-noindex,header.l-header robots-noindex,div.robots-noindex,header.robots-noindex,div.site-toggle robots-noindex,a.skip-main robots-noindex,div.header-nav robots-noindex,div.browsenav robots-noindex,div.browsenav browsenav-stuck robots-noindex,div.row robots-noindex,div.footer robots-noindex,div.row oss-nocrawl,div.skip-main oss-nocrawl
property.description: A comma-delimited list of css like tags to identify the elements which should NOT be parsed. Use this to tell the HTML parser to ignore the given elements, e.g. site navigation. It is allowed to only specify the element type (required), and optional its class name ('.') or ID ('#'). More complex expressions will not be parsed. Valid examples: div.header,span,p#test,div#main,ul,div.footercol Invalid expressions: div#head#part1,#footer,.inner#post Note that the elements and their children will be silently ignored by the parser, so verify the indexed content with Luke to confirm results. Use either 'parser.html.blacklist' or 'parser.html.whitelist', but not both of them at once. If so, only the whitelist is used.

property.name: parser.html.whitelist
property.description: A comma-delimited list of css like tags to identify the elements which should be parsed. Use this to tell the HTML parser to only use the given elements, e.g. content. It is allowed to only specify the element type (required), and optional its class name ('.') or ID ('#'). More complex expressions will not be parsed. Valid examples: div.header,span,p#test Invalid expressions: div#head#part1,#footer,.inner#post Note that the elements and their children will be silently ignored by the parser, so verify the indexed content with Luke to confirm results. Use either 'parser.html.blacklist' or 'parser.html.whitelist', but not both of them at once. If so, only the whitelist is used.

property.name: parser.html.text.blacklist
property.description: A piped-delimited list type,id,class prefix and comma-delimated list of values in parenthesis to identify the elements which should NOT be parsed. Use this to tell the HTML parser to ignore the given elements, e.g. site navigation. Valid examples: type(div,span,p,ul)|id(test,main)|class(header,footercol) Note that the elements and their children will be silently ignored by the parser, so verify the indexed content with Luke to confirm results. Use either 'parser.html.blacklist' or 'parser.html.whitelist', but not both of them at once. If so, only the whitelist is used.
